meta.title: How to set up business email on your own domain
meta.description: Step by step to professional email on your domain: the DNS records, mailboxes for the team and switching providers without losing mail.

custom-domain-email.card: What you need, the DNS records and how to switch providers without losing mail.
custom-domain-email.title: How to set up business email on your own domain
custom-domain-email.lead: An address like you@yourcompany.com earns more trust than a free webmail account, and it stays yours if you change providers. This guide covers the whole path: what you need, the DNS records and how to switch without losing mail.

sections.title: What you need
body: A registered domain, for example at GoDaddy, Namecheap, Hostinger or Cloudflare, and access to its DNS settings.
A service that receives and sends email for your domain. In MepMail that is Mail: mailboxes on your domain, with no server to install or maintain.

sections.title: Step by step
steps: Create your MepMail account and add your domain in the dashboard.

Publish the DNS records the dashboard shows: a DKIM TXT (mepmail._domainkey), the MX and SPF of the bounce subdomain and, to receive, the domain's MX. If your DNS is on Cloudflare, MepMail can create the records with a DNS-only token, without overwriting existing ones.
Wait for verification. The dashboard checks each record live and shows what is missing; it usually takes minutes to a few hours.
Create the mailboxes: one per person or for an AI agent. Plans go from 1 to 10 mailboxes.
Once the MX points to MepMail, turn receiving on in Mail → Receiving. The dashboard checks the MX before it switches on.
Read and reply in the browser or in the MepMail app for Windows and Linux.

sections.title: Already on another provider? Switch without losing mail
body: First create every mailbox and alias the domain receives, and only then change the MX. That way no message is left without a destination during the switch.
Then bring the old account's history over: Mail imports your messages over IMAP.

sections.title: What it costs
body: In MepMail, Mail starts at US$ 2.90 a month on the Solo plan, with 1 mailbox. Duo has 3 mailboxes for US$ 5.90 and Equipe has 10 for US$ 12.90.
Your first purchase starts with 7 days free (a card is required), and nothing is charged beyond the plan.

sections.title: What about AI agents?
body: A mailbox can belong to a person or to an agent. The agent reads and drafts over MCP or the API, only with the permissions you grant, and sending can wait for your approval.

faq.q: Do I need a mail server?
faq.a: No. MepMail receives, stores and sends for you; on your side there are only the domain's DNS records.

faq.q: How long does it take to work?
faq.a: Records usually apply within minutes; some DNS providers take a few hours. The dashboard shows each record's status meanwhile.

faq.q: Will I lose email when I switch providers?
faq.a: Not if you create the mailboxes before pointing the MX. Messages already at the old provider can be imported over IMAP.

faq.q: Does it work on my phone?
faq.a: Yes, in the browser. The installed app is for Windows and Linux.

cta.title: Your email on your domain, from US$ 2.90 a month
cta.body: Try it for 7 days and set up your domain with the dashboard's step by step.

meta.title: SPF, DKIM and DMARC: what they are and how to set them up
meta.description: Understand SPF, DKIM and DMARC, the records that get your email into the inbox, and how to set them up in your domain's DNS.

email-authentication.card: The three records that tell providers the email is really yours, and how to publish each one.
email-authentication.title: SPF, DKIM and DMARC: what they are and how to set them up
email-authentication.lead: Three DNS records tell Gmail, Outlook and other providers that a message with your domain really came from you. Without them, your email tends to land in spam or get rejected.

sections.title: Why it matters
body: Since 2024, Gmail and Yahoo require every sender to authenticate the domain with SPF or DKIM. Bulk senders (more than 5,000 messages a day to Gmail accounts) need all three: SPF, DKIM and DMARC.
Beyond delivery, these records protect your brand: they make it harder for anyone to send fake email in your domain's name.

sections.title: SPF: who may send for your domain
body: SPF is a TXT record listing the servers allowed to send for the domain. Each domain name should have a single SPF record; if you use more than one service, merge their includes into one record.
In MepMail, SPF lives on the bounce subdomain (MAIL FROM), which the dashboard creates and shows next to its MX.

sections.title: DKIM: the signature on every message
body: DKIM signs each message with a private key; the public key sits in a TXT record in your DNS, and the receiving provider checks the signature.
In MepMail, new domains use a single TXT at mepmail._domainkey, shown in the dashboard when you add the domain.

sections.title: DMARC: what to do when something fails
body: DMARC is a TXT at _dmarc.yourdomain.com. It tells providers what to do with messages that pass neither SPF nor DKIM aligned with the sender's domain, and where to send reports.
Start by monitoring, with v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc@yourdomain.com, read the reports for a few weeks, then move to p=quarantine and, if you like, p=reject.

sections.title: How to check
body: The MepMail dashboard resolves each record live and shows, line by line, what is fine and what is missing, including the DMARC inherited from the parent domain when you send from a subdomain.
To check a delivered message, open the original in Gmail (Show original): spf=pass, dkim=pass and dmarc=pass mean you are all set.

faq.q: Can I have two SPF records?
faq.a: No. Two SPF records on the same name invalidate both; merge the services into a single record.

faq.q: Will DMARC with p=reject block my email?
faq.a: Only messages that fail aligned authentication. That is why the safe path is to start with p=none and raise the policy after reading the reports.

faq.q: Do I need this if I only receive email?
faq.a: Yes, it is recommended: SPF and DMARC make it harder for others to spoof your domain.

cta.title: Set up your domain with live verification
cta.body: MepMail shows every missing record and checks your DNS while you publish.

meta.title: Transactional email: what it is and how to send it from your app
meta.description: What transactional email is (sign-up, password, receipt), why to keep it apart from marketing and how to send it by API or SMTP without spam.

transactional-email.card: Sign-up, password and receipt: how it differs from marketing and how to send it by API or SMTP.
transactional-email.title: Transactional email: what it is and how to send it from your app
transactional-email.lead: Transactional email is what your app sends because the user did something: created an account, asked for a new password, bought. It has to arrive fast and in the inbox.

sections.title: Examples
body: Sign-up confirmation, password reset, verification code, receipt, shipping notice and account alerts.

sections.title: Transactional is not marketing
body: Newsletters and promotions depend on consent and need an easy unsubscribe. Transactional email is expected by the user, so it has its own rules and reputation.
Keep the two apart, for example with different senders or subdomains, so a poorly received campaign does not hurt your password email.

sections.title: How to send: API or SMTP
body: With the HTTP API you get each message's id, can use an idempotency key so nothing goes out twice, and follow delivery, bounces and complaints through webhooks. The MepMail API is compatible with the Resend SDK.
With SMTP, any system that already speaks SMTP works, from WordPress to an ERP: in MepMail the relay is smtp.mepmail.dev, on port 2587 with STARTTLS.

sections.title: Good practices
steps: Authenticate the domain with SPF, DKIM and DMARC.
Use one idempotency key per message, so a retry never sends twice.
Respect bounces and complaints: stop sending to addresses that bounced permanently.
Keep marketing out of the transactional flow.

sections.title: What it costs
body: In MepMail, Send is free up to 100 emails a day, no card. Pro sends 110,000 emails a month for US$ 29.

faq.q: Can I use Gmail's SMTP in my app?
faq.a: Personal accounts have low daily limits and are not made for apps; a sending service gives you deliverability, logs and webhooks.
The API when you write the code: message id, idempotency and webhooks. SMTP when the system already has an SMTP server field.

faq.q: Do I need my own domain?
faq.a: Yes. The authenticated domain is what gets the message into the inbox.

cta.title: Start sending for free
cta.body: 100 emails a day with no card, by API, SMTP or MCP.

meta.title: How an AI agent sends and reads email over MCP
meta.description: Connect Claude, Cursor or another MCP client to MepMail: the hosted OAuth server or the npm package, the mail tools and the permissions.

ai-agent-email-mcp.card: The hosted OAuth server, the npm package, the mail tools an agent reads and answers with, and the permissions that keep sending under control.
ai-agent-email-mcp.title: How an AI agent sends and reads email over MCP
ai-agent-email-mcp.lead: An agent can write the message; sending it still needs a server that checks the sending domain, the quota and the suppressions. MepMail's MCP server gives the agent those tools, on the same pipeline as the REST API.

sections.title: Two ways to connect
body: The hosted server at https://api.mepmail.dev/mcp speaks Streamable HTTP and signs in with OAuth, so no key is pasted into the client's config.
The npm package @mepmail/mcp speaks stdio and reaches your instance with a team key or a mailbox key, for clients that launch servers from a config file.
The names and the result shape are the same on both, so a prompt written for one works on the other; the hosted server also exposes the tools that manage domains, webhooks, templates and broadcasts.

sections.title: Option 1: the hosted server, with OAuth
steps: In Claude Code, run the command below, then /mcp and pick mepmail to sign in. Add --scope user to make it available in every project.
In Cursor, add the URL to .cursor/mcp.json in the project, or to ~/.cursor/mcp.json for every project.
In VS Code, add it to .vscode/mcp.json with type http and the URL.
In Claude Desktop, add a custom connector under Settings → Connectors, or bridge to the HTTP endpoint with mcp-remote.
On the consent screen, pick the team the client may act on and untick the permissions you do not want to grant. Nothing is copied or pasted.

code.label: Claude Code
code.content: claude mcp add --transport http mepmail https://api.mepmail.dev/mcp

sections.title: Option 2: the local package
body: The package needs Node.js 20 or newer and runs with npx, with no OAuth and no browser step: the config block is the whole install.

Set MEPMAIL_API_KEY for the sending tools, a team key that starts with ms_, and MEPMAIL_MAIL_TOKEN for the mailbox tools, an agent key that starts with mmb_ for one mailbox or mmt_ for several. At least one of the two.
MEPMAIL_BASE_URL points at another instance; leave it out to talk to MepMail Cloud.

sections.title: Reading and answering mail
steps: mailbox_list_accounts lists the mailboxes the credential reaches, with their permissions.

mailbox_list_messages returns one page, newest first: pass the returned nextCursor as cursor until hasMore is false, and filter on the server with query, from, subject, unread, after and before. A short page never proves a message is absent.
mailbox_read_message returns headers, text, the revision and the attachment metadata.
mailbox_save_draft creates or edits a plain-text draft without sending, and mailbox_send_draft sends it.
Without the send permission, mailbox_send_draft emails you to approve the send, which waits in the dashboard.
On the hosted server, the same mailbox tools answer at https://api.mepmail.dev/mcp/correio with an agent key instead of OAuth.

sections.title: Sending transactional email
body: send_email sends or schedules one message, send_email_batch takes up to 100 in one call, and update_email and cancel_email handle a scheduled one.

For a safe retry, pass an idempotency_key: keep the same key and the same arguments when retrying the same send, and use a new key for a new operation. Keys belong to the team and last 24 hours, and a completed retry replays the original result.
The sending domain has to be verified first: an unverified sender fails send_email exactly as it fails POST /emails.
list_emails and get_email show the status and the last event, delivered, bounced or complained.

sections.title: Permissions, and why the agent asks
body: Each tool needs a scope, such as emails:send, mail:read or mail:draft. Tools whose permissions you untick are never granted, so the client does not see them.
Sending without asking is a separate tick: leave Direct sending off and every send emails you for approval, and ticking mailboxes never turns it on by itself.

Grants are listed under Settings → Connected apps, where you can revoke your own. Revocation lands at the client's next token refresh, within an hour, and a member removed from the team loses access at once.
Tool results arrive in an untrusted_data envelope: subjects, senders and bodies were written by third parties, and the agent is told to treat them as data, never as instructions.
MCP calls share the API's per-minute rate limit.

sections.title: Before you point an agent at a real inbox
steps: Verify the sending domain, and read its records with get_domain before debugging anything else.
Create the mailbox and its agent key in Correio → Settings → Agents: mmb_ for one mailbox, mmt_ for several.
Start with read and drafts: the agent reads, prepares the reply and asks you before sending.
Check the grant under Settings → Connected apps, then send one message to your own address.
Keep the reach to the mailboxes you ticked: a team credential only reaches the ones mailbox_list_accounts returns.

faq.q: Does the agent need my password?
faq.a: No. The hosted server uses OAuth: you sign in the browser and the client keeps a token you can revoke under Settings → Connected apps. The npm package uses an API key or a mailbox key.

faq.q: Can it read every mailbox in the team?
faq.a: Only the ones you tick at consent, or the ones the agent key covers. The grant is bound to a single team, and the mail tools answer only for the mailboxes in it.

faq.q: What if a send times out?
faq.a: For mail, call mailbox_send_draft again with the same id and revision: that returns the send's status and never sends twice. For transactional email, retry with the same idempotency_key.
Any MCP client. The docs give the config for Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor and VS Code, and the package speaks stdio for everything else.

cta.title: Give your agent a mailbox, not a script
cta.body: Create an account, verify a domain and connect the MCP server in a few minutes.

meta.title: How to send email through the MepMail SMTP relay
meta.description: Point WordPress, a CMS, n8n or your own app at the MepMail SMTP relay: host smtp.mepmail.dev, port 2587 with STARTTLS, user mepmail and a Send key.

smtp-relay-setup.card: The five values a plugin asks for, the limits of the relay, its error codes and a test from the terminal.
smtp-relay-setup.title: How to send email through the MepMail SMTP relay
smtp-relay-setup.lead: Some systems only know how to send email through an SMTP form. The relay takes those messages, checks the domain and the suppressions, and queues them exactly like the API.

sections.title: When the relay is the right door
body: WordPress and WooCommerce with an SMTP plugin, Ghost, Strapi, Supabase Auth, an ERP, a legacy stack: anything that asks for a host, a port, a user and a password instead of an HTTP call.
The relay puts the message through the same accept pipeline as POST /emails: the same domain verification, suppression checks, logs and delivery events.

sections.title: The five values
body: Host: smtp.mepmail.dev.
Port: 2587, with STARTTLS. If the form has an encryption list, choose STARTTLS: the SSL option expects TLS from the first byte, which this port does not speak.
Username: mepmail, fixed for every team. Another name is refused before the key is checked.
Password: a key created under API keys, the one that starts with ms_, ideally one that can only send.
Encryption: STARTTLS before AUTH. Without a TLS keypair the relay does not start, unless the operator explicitly allows plaintext auth on a private network.

code.label: Settings → SMTP
code.content:
Host: smtp.mepmail.dev
Port: 2587
Encryption: STARTTLS
Username: mepmail
Password: ms_... (a Send key)

sections.title: Before the first message: the domain
body: The From address has to be on a domain verified for the team. An unverified domain is refused with 554 before anything is queued.
A key restricted to one domain only sends from that domain, over SMTP as well.
The relay does not take attachments today: a message with one is refused with 554, the same boundary POST /emails has.

sections.title: Paste it in: WordPress, Ghost, n8n
steps: WordPress or WooCommerce: install an SMTP plugin, choose the option for another SMTP server, paste the five values, set the encryption to STARTTLS and send a test to your own address.
Ghost, Strapi and Supabase Auth: the same values in the mail settings, with a From on the verified domain.
n8n: the MepMail community node, n8n-nodes-mepmail, is the first-class path for sending; the relay is there for nodes that only speak SMTP.
Any other system: fill the SMTP section, not the API section, and start with a test message to yourself.

sections.title: What the relay checks, and its limits
steps: One From address, a non-empty Subject, and at least one To recipient that is also an envelope recipient.
Up to 50 recipients per message, and 10 connections from the same IP at once.
A message up to 40 MB; a larger one is refused.
Only envelope recipients receive the message: To and Cc decide who is visible, and the rest are Bcc.
Three failed logins on one connection close it with 421.

sections.title: The error codes you will see
body: 553: a single From address, a non-empty Subject, or a To that is also an envelope recipient is missing.
535: the username is not mepmail, or the password is not a valid key.
554: the From domain is not verified for the team, the sender is disguised, or the message carries an attachment.
550: the team is suspended, every recipient is suppressed, or the key is restricted to another domain.
452: more than 50 recipients, or a sending quota is exhausted, parked backlog included.
552: the message is over the size cap.

sections.title: Test from the terminal
body: Python's standard library is enough to check the credentials and the domain before you touch the app. Replace the key and the two addresses:

code.label: send_test.py
code.content:
import smtplib
from email.message import EmailMessage

msg = EmailMessage()
msg["From"] = "you@yourdomain.com"
msg["To"] = "you@example.com"
msg["Subject"] = "Relay test"
msg.set_content("It works.")

with smtplib.SMTP("smtp.mepmail.dev", 2587) as smtp:
    smtp.starttls()
    smtp.login("mepmail", "ms_...")
    smtp.send_message(msg)

faq.a: Use 2587 with STARTTLS. That is the port the relay listens on, and STARTTLS is the encryption it offers.
A Send key, the one that starts with ms_. The username stays mepmail for every team and every key.

faq.q: How do I know it worked?
faq.a: A successful send answers Queued as an id in the SMTP reply, and the message appears under Emails with the same events as an API send.
Not yet. The relay refuses a message with an attachment (554), the same limit POST /emails has; send a link to the file instead.

cta.title: Put your app on the relay
cta.body: Create an account, verify the domain and create a Send key. The same values are in Settings → SMTP.
